summary: Inspected all 42 Lean files in the review unit. Every file contains formal mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and complete proofs with no `sorry` axioms. The files cover: the almost-everywhere view of graphons and its compatibility with cut norm, cut distance, and homomorphism densities (AEEqFun/Basic.lean, Validation.lean); the counting lemma and its coupling/cut-distance forms (Counting.lean); cut distance to constant and point-mass graphons (CutMetric/Constant.lean); the overlaid difference kernel and its properties (CutMetric/Coupling.lean); the coupling-primary cut distance and its basic laws (CutMetric/Distance.lean); rounding finite weighted graphs onto grids (CutMetric/OfMatrixGrid.lean); the map form of the cut distance and its agreement with the coupling form (CutMetric/Pullback/Basic.lean, Constant.lean, Validation.lean); the triangle inequality for graphon cut distance (CutMetric/Triangle.lean); extreme exchangeable graph laws (ExchangeableGraphLaw/Extreme.lean); cut-norm limits of graphon sequences (Graphon/CutNormLimit.lean); total boundedness of graphon space (GraphonSpace/TotallyBounded.lean); closeness of finite homomorphism densities (HomDensity/Closeness.lean); the cut norm of symmetric kernels (Kernel/CutNorm.lean); graph parameters, connection matrices, and reflection positivity (Representability/ConnectionMatrix.lean, Validation.lean); concentration of sampled homomorphism densities (Sampling/Concentration.lean); finite and infinite sampling from graphons (Sampling/Finite.lean, Infinite.lean); point sampling and Bernoulli edge rounding (Sampling/PointSampling.lean, Rounding.lean); finite graphs as graphons (StepGraphon/FiniteGraph/Basic.lean, Validation.lean); transversals of fixed-point-free involutions (Enumerative/InvolutionTransversal.lean); loops and their excursions (Enumerative/LoopWord.lean); occurrence and transition counts of finite words (Enumerative/TransitionCount.lean); quotienting permutation triples by blocks (PermutationTriple/BlockQuotient.lean); generating counts by cycle type (PermutationTriple/GeneratingCount.lean); examples of passports and their enumeration (PermutationTriple/Passport/Examples.lean); indexed quiver paths and partial concatenation (Quiver/TotalPath.lean); measurability of simple graphs and relabelling (SimpleGraph/Measurable.lean); finite trees of maximum degree two as path graphs (SimpleGraph/PathGraph.lean); the Bender-Knuth involutions (Young/BenderKnuth.lean); beta-numbers of Young diagrams (Young/BetaNumbers.lean); the Frobenius determinant formula and hook-length formula (Young/HookLength/Formula.lean); interlacing shapes and the branching rule (Young/Interlacing.lean); rim hooks of Young diagrams (Young/RimHook.lean); the Robinson-Schensted correspondence (Young/RobinsonSchensted.lean, Schensted.lean); and partitions with Young diagrams (Young/Partitions.lean). Per FILTER-002/004/007/021, hard exclusion requires evidence that no unique formal mathematics is lost; that threshold is not met for any file. All files define substantive combinatorial/analytic structures and prove nontrivial theorems about them.
